title: Working with Assets and Global Styles knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Working with Assets and Global Styles”?
options: Working with Assets and Global Styles means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Working with Assets and Global Styles removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Working with Assets and Global Styles should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Working with Assets and Global Styles helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Working with Assets and Global Styles helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Working with Assets and Global Styles is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Static assets” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Static assets” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Static assets” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Static assets” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Static assets” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Static assets” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Static assets” under Working with Assets and Global Styles. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Working with Assets and Global Styles”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
